title: Trolley Problem
body:
The **trolley problem** presents a choice between acting to cause one death and refraining
while five die. It exists to separate the frameworks, because they answer it differently and
the difference is the whole point of the exercise.

```
[[Utilitarianism]]   five lives against one, so pull the lever
[[Kantianism]]       pulling the lever uses the one person as a means to
                     save the five, which the second formulation prohibits
```

Its technological form is concrete. An autonomous vehicle facing an unavoidable collision
behaves according to code written months earlier by an engineer who was not present, so the
decision is made in advance, deliberately, by somebody who has time to think about it. That
removes the usual defence that a human driver reacted by instinct.

Three features make the engineering version harder than the philosophy version. The decision is
made once and applied to every future case. It is made by a company, and the person at risk is
somebody else entirely. And it becomes a specification, so it can be read, audited and
litigated, which no instinct can.

The course uses it as the entry point to [[Ethical Analysis]] because it is the cleanest
case where two respectable frameworks give opposite answers with no ambiguity about the facts.
